evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, 歡 entry
evidence.field: 說文 / 形義通解 / 字例 / historical uses
evidence.text: The entry gives the traditional graph as 从欠、雚聲 and glosses its basic sense as happiness or joy. It lists 《書·洛誥》“公功肅將祗歡,” 《史記·田敬仲完世家》“陽生素與乞歡” (being on friendly terms), and 《樂府詩集·子夜歌》“自從別歡來” (a lover addressed as 歡). It also lists a later sense of doing something vigorously, with a Tang 王涯 poem. The entry shows 小篆 and bamboo/silk examples, but its 金文 and 甲骨 sections contain no examples; this supports only a gap in this database’s displayed evidence, not proof that the graph did not exist earlier.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, 歡 entry
evidence.field: A02065-001 entry and cited variant references
evidence.text: The dictionary classifies 欢 as a variant of 歡 and says 歡 is written in Shuowen as 喜樂也、從欠，雚聲. It cites 宋元以來俗字譜 entries from 目連記 and 金瓶梅 for 欢, and 字學三正’s statement 歡，俗作欢. This supports a pre-modern variant history for 欢; it does not establish that its modern status as the standardized simplified form began in those texts.
evidence.title: [A02065] 歡 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, 欠 entry
evidence.text: The entry cites Shuowen’s account of 欠 as a person opening the mouth and breathing/yawning, with the form depicting qi emerging above a person. Later listed meanings include raising or moving the body slightly and deficiency. Shuowen’s definition of 欠 does not itself say that it depicts laughter; assigning an additional laughter-related nuance in 歡 is an interpretation, not a directly attested explanation in this source.
evidence.title: [A02052] 欠 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 《說文解字》大徐本 and 段注本
evidence.text: Shuowen’s 雚 entry calls the referent 小爵 and analyzes the graph as 从雈、吅聲, citing 詩曰「雚鳴于垤」. Duan Yucai emends the received gloss 小爵 to 雚爵/雀 and identifies the bird with 鸛; he notes that the received text of the poem has 鸛 and that 雚 is another textual form. Thus the bird gloss and the precise referent are textually disputed; the character 雚 has documented bird-related use, but this evidence does not recover an exact spoken name that would independently prove any loan claim.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary with textual variant discussion
evidence.title: 雚的说文解字解释

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, official Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1
evidence.field: radical/stroke table page 70, 雚 row; verified against local sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1144
evidence.text: The official table gives 雚 guàn, Middle Chinese kwanH, Old Chinese *C.qʷˤar-s, gloss heron. The local TSV row agrees exactly. This offers an independently listed pronunciation and bird gloss for the 雚 graph, but does not establish that this is the source pronunciation meant when 雚 functions as a phonetic in 歡.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, official Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1
evidence.field: radical/stroke table page 70, 歡 row; verified against local sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1350
evidence.text: The official table gives 歡 huān, Middle Chinese xwan (x- + -wan A), Old Chinese *qʷʰˤar, gloss rejoice; joyous. The local TSV matches. Comparing readings within this one system, 歡 *qʷʰˤar and 雚 *C.qʷˤar-s share a close onset and rhyme, consistent with a phonetic role despite different prefixes and suffixes. This is a phonological comparison, not evidence that the noun for the bird was borrowed as the word for rejoicing.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Research of Unearthed Texts and Ancient Characters, Lei Xieren on 洛誥
evidence.field: discussion of 公功肅將祗歡 and alternative readings
evidence.text: The scholarly commentary documents disagreement over how to parse and understand the 洛誥 phrase: older interpreters take 歡 with a joy-related sense, while other proposals read it as 灌 or 勸 and assign different syntax and meanings. The commentator favors reading 歡 as 勸 in this passage. Accordingly, this early textual token is evidence for a transmitted graph in the passage, but its precise sense is disputed and should not be treated as an unambiguous early attestation of ordinary ‘joy’ without qualification.
evidence.title: 雷燮仁：《尚書集注試解·洛誥》（徵求意見稿）

evidence.source: Chinese Wikisource transcription of 宋元以來俗字譜
evidence.field: 欠部 table, 歡 and 歎 rows
evidence.text: The table’s 歡 row lists several graph variants across named literary sources; the following continuation row includes 欢 under 目連記 and 金瓶梅. This corroborates use of 欢 as a pre-modern variant in those source texts, but the table does not supply composition dates for each text or manuscript witness, so no precise first-use date is established here.
evidence.title: 宋元以來俗字譜/木部至欠部

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, publication record for 宋元以來俗字譜
evidence.text: The Institute says 宋元以來俗字譜 was compiled in 1929 from twelve works, covering examples from the Song/Yuan period onward, and first published in 1930. This dates the compilation and gives the broad scope of its source corpus, not the exact occurrence date of every listed form.
evidence.title: Latest Publications: 宋元以來俗字譜

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, 歡 entry
evidence.field: 廣韻 and historical use summary
evidence.text: The entry records 呼官 as the fanqie for 歡 and identifies its Guangyun category as level tone, 山 division, 桓 rhyme, closed, division I. It reports the citation on page 126. This is a later medieval pronunciation record; its broad rhyme and onset evidence accords with the Middle Chinese xwan transcription in the Baxter system, but the notation systems should remain distinct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database lists 欢 as U+6B22, gives its six-stroke form and readings huan1/tan4, and describes it as the simplified form of 歡 as well as a variant of 歎. The second association warns that graphic identity across contexts does not mean all occurrences of 欢 have the joyful-word reading.
evidence.title: 漢字「欢」：基本資料

gaps: No visually inspected glyph images are claimed. The consulted CUHK character entry shows seal-script and bamboo/silk examples but no listed oracle-bone or bronze examples; this is a database coverage gap and does not prove nonexistence.

The earliest secure date for the 歡 graph itself is unresolved. The 洛誥 passage is early textual material but its specific phrase is disputed, including proposals to read 歡 as 勸 or 灌; its transmitted wording alone does not establish an unambiguous early everyday sense.

The exact earliest dated occurrence of the simplified-looking form 欢 is unresolved. Official Taiwan variant-dictionary citations establish pre-modern俗字 usage in named works but do not supply occurrence dates or manuscript witness dates in the inspected entry.

The proposed laughter nuance for semantic 欠 is not established by the inspected sources. Shuowen defines 欠 as mouth-opening/breathing/yawning, and the graph may classify an oral or bodily expression; the added ‘joyfully laughing’ explanation remains interpretive.

The exact historical pictorial referent and pronunciation of 雚 are not independently settled: Shuowen’s 小爵 wording is emended by Duan Yucai, while Baxter–Sagart list the reading *C.qʷˤar-s and gloss it ‘heron.’ This uncertainty limits an object-name borrowing claim, but does not undermine the independently supported phonetic role of 雚 in 歡.

Zhengzhang Shangfang *qʰoːn and Baxter–Sagart *qʷʰˤar are separate system-specific proposals. The local TSV is Baxter–Sagart and matches the official table; do not substitute the Zhengzhang value into its field.
No evidence found that 歡 was borrowed as a whole graph for another word; research supports treating the proposed 雚 as a phonetic component in a phono-semantic graph, not as a whole-graph loan.
